# reac-pw / fuzz_link

reac-pw's own fuzz target `fuzz_link` ([source](source/fuzz_link.c), unmodified), which OSS-Fuzz does not run, over reac-pw 1.0.42 (FreeREAC/reac-pw at f86a30a3).

Runs a sequence of input-chosen operations against a fake kernel netlink socket: read an interface's alias and link kind, write an alias, mark and unmark served interfaces, and decide a verdict from a kind and alias; checks requests, return codes, buffer bounds, socket use and the kept marks against a model of the kernel and the marking policy. The harness points the marking code's messages at a fixed buffer in memory, so the run writes none of them; no check depends on them.

## How this program differs from a libFuzzer build of this fuzz target
- Linked against a static library of reac-pw's nine input readers and the harness's box-model table, built from source with libreac's and PipeWire SPA's headers only; neither library is linked. The netlink reader is compiled with its socket calls renamed to the harness's fake kernel, as the project's own fuzz build does.
- In every build, getenv() returns NULL, getpid() returns 1 and mkstemp() uses a fixed name, so the program depends only on its input.
- A small driver reads the input file, calls the fuzz target one to four times and prints each return value.

## What the harness checks
- Every socket the reader opens it closes before it returns, and it sends, receives and closes only that socket ([lines 487-496](source/fuzz_link.c#L487-L496)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- Each operation sends exactly the netlink requests it owes, in order and byte for byte ([lines 498-517](source/fuzz_link.c#L498-L517)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- A read or write that cannot be made (no name, an empty name, an alias too long, an interface with no index) opens no socket ([lines 519-530](source/fuzz_link.c#L519-L530)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- A read answers the reply's code, and on success the link kind and alias the reply carries, cut to the buffers ([lines 532-553](source/fuzz_link.c#L532-L553)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- A text written into a buffer ends in a NUL inside it, and the byte after the buffer is unchanged ([lines 555-566](source/fuzz_link.c#L555-L566)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- A write answers the reply's code, and refuses an alias too long for the kernel with -ENAMETOOLONG ([lines 568-577](source/fuzz_link.c#L568-L577)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- The verdict on an interface follows its alias (one set by the host is left alone, one of this daemon's is its own), then its link kind ([lines 579-593](source/fuzz_link.c#L579-L593)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- A mark answers its verdict, or the error of the read or write that stopped it, and -EINVAL with no marks or no name ([lines 595-606](source/fuzz_link.c#L595-L606)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- The marks kept are the interfaces this daemon marked, or found marked by an earlier run of its own, each once, at most 32; the unmark clears them all ([lines 608-623](source/fuzz_link.c#L608-L623)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.

Each build also links code that no sanitizer instruments, as its link recorded it. A statement about a sanitizer build covers that code only as uninstrumented code: ASan checks no load or store made inside it, and UBSan inserts no check there.

- plain: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library)
- ubsan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library)
- asan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.asan.a` (the sanitizer runtime), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library), `libunwind.a` (the C++ runtime)
